definition: Retrograde memory is memory for information from the past, especially events and knowledge from before the onset of an illness or injury. Loss of retrograde memory means difficulty recalling previously stored memories while the ability to learn new information may remain normal.

reasons: The packet does not define “retrograde memory” as a general term; it only mentions “loss of retrograde memory” in the context of focal retrograde amnesia and related case reports.

The phrase “especially events and knowledge from before the onset of an illness or injury” is not supported by the packet and imports a clinical framing that is not stated as a definition of the term.

The final sentence shifts the term toward a disorder description (“loss of retrograde memory” with normal new learning), which the packet supports only as a feature of focal retrograde amnesia, not as the definition of retrograde memory itself.
The packet does not provide a direct definition of “retrograde memory” as memory for information from the past (e.g., events/knowledge before illness or injury).

The statement that loss of retrograde memory corresponds to difficulty recalling previously stored memories while learning new information may remain normal is only indirectly supported by the packet’s contrast between retrograde memory loss and “normal learning of new information,” but the packet does not explicitly define this as “retrograde memory” in general or affirm the “may remain normal” phrasing as a general rule.
